<!-- pr-reviewer: a08c5815854e4d271591dc2fb17b32d68b3e40c0 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers. The PR is a draft. The author flags it ready when the v0.26.0 cut allows it.

Review tier: safety floor (P1, posted G-code). Built locally, on a trial merge of head `a08c58158` with `origin/main` `d0327d187`. The merge was clean.

### What looks good

- All six posts use the same helper pair as the Mach4 fix (#3731) and the Haas fix (#3694). The pair is `tapFeed` plus `tapPitchHolds`. It has the same 1e-4 tolerance and the same refusal text. The written F goes back through the same formatter, and the written S goes through `Math.round`. This is the S word that `ni(sRpm)` writes.
- The precision is correct in each post: three decimals in mm/min and four decimals in in/min. The trailing zeros are removed. The Fanuc family (`fanuc`, `doosan-dnm`, `mazak`) uses `pt(fn())` and keeps its point. `sinumerik`, `tormach` and `linuxcnc` use `fu()`, with no forced point.
- The refusal comes before `xyFirst`, so a refused tap writes no move. The operation name is in the message. A NaN feed or a zero feed also fails the `want > 0` check and is refused. In `fanuc.cps`, the M29 refusal (no spindle speed) still runs first.
- Only the G84 F word changes. All other feeds keep `fw()`/`ff()`, which the decision file says (#3690 owns them). Only the six named posts change.
- After this PR, each post on main that writes G84 holds the pitch. The other posts (`mach3`, `grbl`, `grblhal`, `richauto`, `tinyg`) refuse G84 by name.
- The pins are red-first. I put back main's six `.cps` files in the trial-merge tree and ran `tap_feed_mill_posts`: 6 failed, each with `left: Some("F35")`, `right: Some("F34.5")`. With the PR's posts: 6 passed.
- The pin file is in `crates/post/tests/`, the lowest crate that provides what it imports, and its Gate map names the six posts. The pins cover both feeds from the issue, a three-decimal feed, a whole feed with and without the point, two inch feeds, a fractional-rpm refusal and an inch underflow refusal.
- All eight golden changes are on G84 lines only. The PR body explains each change.
- The decision file cites no HSMWorks or Autodesk material. It gives our own issues (#1836, #3690, #3701) as its reasons.

### Results merged with main (locally, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`, `-j 6`)

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test tap_feed_mill_posts` | 6 passed |
| Same pins with main's six posts (red-first) | 6 failed (`F35` vs `F34.5`) |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post --no-fail-fast` (140 binaries, all post suites) | 1200 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test conformance` | 7 passed (`every_builtin_posts_every_golden_byte_exact` included) |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Heavy lanes

`cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches 62 app heavy steps, because a post script maps widely. No pin needs a heavy step. The author ran one targeted heavy step on this head: `app heavy: example_catalog`, ok (PR body). This review ran no heavy step. The other reached lanes run at the cut. This follows the maintainer's order for heavy lanes at review (targeted steps only, full heavy at the cut).

### Requested before merge

None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)

1. Inch tap feed on the Fanuc family: the G84 F word now has four decimals in in/min (for example `F1.3583`). Please confirm that a Fanuc, Doosan or Mazak control in G20/G94 reads the fourth decimal and does not cut it to 0.01 in/min. If one does, the pitch check passes but the control cuts a different pitch. The safe fix for that case is to compare the pitch with the feed at the control's real F step. LinuxCNC and PathPilot read the full decimal.
2. The decision file cites no external public source for the decimal-point statements, for example that Sinumerik reads a decimal F as written. A reference to the Siemens ISO-dialect document that `sinumerik.cps` already cites would make the statement traceable. This is optional.
3. The refusal text says "feed N mm/min" also in an inch program. This is the same text as Mach4 and Haas, so it stays consistent. I note it only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
